chunks: Yahya al-Halabi from Bashir al-Kunasi who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying:

You maintained relations whilst the people cut-off, and you loved whilst the people hated, and you recognized whilst the people denied, and it is the Truth. Indeed, Allah took Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a servant before He took him as a Prophet, and indeed Ali (peace be upon him) was a servant, sincere to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so He was sincere to Him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loved him, and he loved Him.

Surely, our rights in the Book of Allah are clear. For us is the pure wealth, and for us is the Spoils of War (Al-Anfal), and we are a people whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated obedience to, and you follow those whom people have no excuse for their ignorance regarding. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever dies and has no Imam for him, has died the death of ignorance. Upon you is obedience, for you have seen the companions of Ali (peace be upon him).'

Then he said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said during his illness in which he passed away: 'Call my friend for me!'. So two (females) sent for their respective fathers, but when they came, he turned his face away, then said: 'Call my friend for me!'. They said, 'He would have looked at us had he intended to speak to us'. So they sent for Ali (peace be upon him). So when he came, he leaned across towards him, and he narrated to him, and narrated to him, until he finished. So they met him and said, 'What did he narrate to you?' He said: 'He narrated to me by a thousand doors of knowledge, each door of which opens to a thousand doors'.

key_terms.أَلْفِ بَابٍ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ: A thousand doors of knowledge (referring to the vastness of Ali's knowledge)
key_terms.إِمَامٌ: Imam (leader/guide, specifically referring to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْأَنْفَالُ: The Spoils of War (a specific category of wealth in Islamic law)
key_terms.الْحَقُّ: The Truth (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt or their status)
key_terms.خَلِيلِي: My friend (a term of intimacy and closeness used for Ali)
key_terms.صَفْوُ الْأَمْوَالِ: The pure/clean wealth (referring to Khums or specific wealth rights)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet calling Ali his 'friend' on his deathbed, and what does it reveal about Ali's knowledge?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi underscores the theological foundation of Imam Ali’s authority by contrasting the Ahl al-Bayt’s deep recognition of truth with the people’s ignorance, framing obedience to them as a divine obligation. It further elucidates the concept of 'Ilm al-Ladunni' (divine knowledge) through the deathbed account, where the Prophet’s preference for Ali signifies his exclusive inheritance of prophetic wisdom, a key tenet in Shia exegesis of the Verse of Purification and the Verse of Mubahala.
